run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T17:42:24Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend is backed by real error spans: frontend error spans were zero until 17:42:24, then climbed to ~1161 errored spans per 20m by 17:57:24, and every errored frontend operation belongs to the checkout path (POST /api/checkout -> grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder -> checkout PlaceOrder -> shipping /get-quote -> shipping client span 'POST quote' -> quote POST /getquote). The deepest observed failure is shipping's outbound HTTP call to the quote Service: all errored 'POST quote' client spans last between 5s and 10s, versus 1.8-14.9ms for the same span in a pre-incident baseline trace, while the successful calls in the same 10 minutes are spread up to 5s (10.5/23.3 under 10ms, 17.5/23.3 under 1.4s). The quote application itself is not the failing component: its own server spans stay fast (20.9 of 23.3 under 2ms, 22.1 under 10ms), it emits no error-status spans, its CPU is ~0.0009 cores against a 5m limit, its memory is ~17-18MB against 40Mi, its throttling ratio declines through the incident, and its logs show bulk 'Calculated quote' lines stop after ~17:40 while shipping logs show repeated 'Requesting quote' lines with no reply after 17:50:26. Both quote pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, the Service has both pod IPs as endpoints, and the frontend request rate was flat at ~54 spans/s from 17:24 to 17:52, so neither a quote restart/rollout nor a load ramp explains the 17:42 onset. The evidence therefore localizes the fault to the shipping-to-quote request path (transport/connection setup) rather than to quote's application code or resource limits, but the specific object at fault could not be identified: packet-level, DNS and node-level telemetry are absent and Jaeger has no traces after ~17:26:30, so no error text or HTTP status for the incident is available.

claims.text: frontend error spans are absent before the incident: sum by status_code of increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend"}[20m]) is 0 at every step from 17:20:24 to 17:41:24, first becomes non-zero at 17:42:24 (111.0) and rises to 1161.6 by 17:57:24, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans simultaneously fall from a 56883 peak (17:40:24) to 36665 (17:57:24).

Per-service error onset is sequential along the call chain: frontend's first non-zero 5m error increase is at 17:42:00 (120.0), and checkout and shipping both first become non-zero at 17:43:00 with identical values (94.5412), then track each other exactly (e.g. 311.111 at 17:48:00, 304.444 at 17:50:00, 145.884 at 17:54:00), while ad, fraud-detection and recommendation stay at their ~1.11 pre-incident background level and accounting, cart and payment remain at 0.

At 17:57:24 the 20m error increase by service and span is: frontend POST /api/checkout 290.41, frontend executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 290.41, frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 290.41, frontend POST 290.41 (total 1161.6); checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 266.82 and checkout HTTP POST 266.82; shipping /get-quote 266.82 and shipping POST quote 266.82; frontend-proxy ingress 296.65 and router frontend egress 292.49. No service_name="quote" series exists with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR.

A pre-incident baseline trace (checkout PlaceOrder, 17:26:29) shows the normal chain load-generator -> frontend-proxy ingress/router frontend egress -> frontend POST /api/checkout -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder -> checkout HTTP POST -> shipping /get-quote -> shipping POST quote -> quote POST /getquote, all with http.status_code 200 / rpc.grpc.status_code 0, and shipping POST quote durations of 1847us and 14915us with quote POST /getquote of 393us and 439us.

All errored shipping 'POST quote' client spans during 17:47:24-17:57:24 fall above the 5000ms bucket and below/at the 10000ms bucket: increase of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name="shipping",span_name="POST quote",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} is 0 for le=2,4,6,8,10,50,100,200,400,800,1400,2000,5000 and 100.0934 for le=10000 and le=15000 and le=+Inf.

Successful shipping 'POST quote' spans in the same 17:47:24-17:57:24 window are shifted but capped: 23.2775 total, 3.4916 <=2ms, 9.3110 <=4ms, 10.4749 <=10ms, 11.6388 <=50ms, 12.8026 <=100ms, 13.9665 <=200ms and <=800ms, 17.4581 <=1400ms and <=2000ms, 23.2775 <=5000ms and <=+Inf, so some successful calls still took 1.4-5s while none exceeded 5s.

The quote service's own server spans are fast throughout the incident: increase of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name="quote",span_name="POST /getquote"} for 17:47:24-17:57:24 is 23.2775 total, 20.9498 <=2ms, 22.1136 <=4/6/8/10ms, and 23.2775 <=100ms/<=+Inf.

shipping's calls to quote changed from all-success to mostly-error while attempt volume stayed roughly constant: 5m increase of shipping 'POST quote' is 200.0 success / 0 error at 17:25:00-17:41:00, then 147.78 success vs 47.27 error at 17:43:00, 62.22 vs 103.72 at 17:45:00, 25.12 vs 129.05 at 17:47:00, 41.11 vs 152.22 at 17:51:00, 23.21 vs 99.81 at 17:53:00.

Quote's received traffic collapses while shipping keeps trying: increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="quote"}[20m]) for POST /getquote, calculate-quote and {closure} falls from 682.82 at 17:42:24 to 507.69 at 17:47:24, 353.27 at 17:52:24 and 187.36 at 17:57:24, and all quote series carry status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET only.

Both quote pods' application logs stop receiving bulk traffic: quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b logs continuous 'Calculated quote' lines until 17:40:25 and quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt until 17:40:25, after which only 1-4 entries per minute appear at approximately :21-:26 of each minute (e.g. sdl5b 17:45:21.777, 17:45:21.970, 17:45:23.478, 17:45:26.129; x9hwt 17:45:21.905, 17:45:22.966, 17:45:23.073, 17:45:25.537).

shipping's application log shows the outbound quote call not completing: at 17:50:22.969-17:50:23.049, 17:50:23.170-17:50:23.175 and 17:50:25.762-17:50:25.780 the sequence 'Requesting quote' -> 'Sending Quote' -> 'Tracking ID Created' completes in 2-80ms, but from 17:50:26.955 onward every line is 'Requesting quote' with no following 'Sending Quote'/'Tracking ID Created' (17:50:26.955, 17:50:27.120, 17:50:27.367, 17:50:27.630, 17:50:29.668 ... 17:50:54.607).

The quote pods are not CPU- or memory-bound: container_cpu_usage_seconds_total for quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b is 0.00061-0.00104 cores and for quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt 0.00053-0.00098 cores, their CFS throttling ratios are 0.05-0.13 and decline after 17:42 (sdl5b 0.1251 at 17:42:24 -> 0.0235 at 17:53:24, x9hwt 0.0578 -> 0.0841), working set is 17.09-18.21MB against a 40Mi limit, and the Deployment limits are cpu 5m / memory 40Mi.

The shipping pod is not resource-bound either: container_cpu_usage_seconds_total for shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 is 0.00012-0.00104 cores against a cpu limit of 5m, its CFS throttling ratio is 0.052-0.135, and its working set is 3.31-3.70MB against a 15Mi limit.

Request volume was flat, not ramping: sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend"}[5m])) is 53.5-54.8 spans/s from 17:24:00 through 17:42:00 and 49.7-51.5 spans/s to 17:52:00, then falls to 40.7 and 23.7 spans/s at 17:54:00 and 17:56:00.

The quote workload is stable and healthy at the object level: Deployment quote has spec.replicas 2 and a single ReplicaSet quote-6b5877698d (created 17:06:14, owner Deployment quote) with 2/2 ready; both pods quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b and quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt are Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and are placed on nodes i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e and i-0f88eaa39b314c60b; all otel-demo pods were created 17:06:14-17:06:16 with 0 restarts.

The quote Service is configured consistently: Service quote is ClusterIP on port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, its Endpoints hold exactly the two quote pod IPs 100.96.2.155 (quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt, node i-0f88eaa39b314c60b) and 100.96.4.53 (quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b, node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e) on port 8080, and shipping's deployment sets QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080.

The quote Deployment defines no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe (container quote, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-quote, port 8080, OTEL_PHP_AUTOLOAD_ENABLED=true, QUOTE_PORT=8080), so pod Ready status does not by itself show that connections are being served.

Node and event state give no resource-pressure signal: all 5 nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure=False and NetworkUnavailable=False, each with capacity/allocatable 4 CPUs and 110 pods; the only events naming a quote pod between 17:40:26 and 17:50:26 are Normal 'Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource' entries at roughly one-minute intervals.

Jaeger's newest available trace data is 2026-11-16T17:26:30, about 32 minutes before the alert, so no span of the failing period is retrievable and the error detail fields of the 17:42+ spans are unavailable.

Network-level telemetry is not present in this Prometheus: the metric-name discovery for {__name__=~"container_network.*|container_memory.*"} returned only container_memory_* names (container_memory_cache, failcnt, failures_total, kernel_usage, max_usage_bytes, rss, total_active_file_bytes, total_inactive_file_bytes, usage_bytes, working_set_bytes) with no container_network_* series, and the discovery {__name__=~"node_.*"} returned only 5 node_namespace_pod_container:* series with no node CPU, load or conntrack metrics.
CoreDNS is up at the time of the query: pods coredns-b5494cbf4-98dwq and coredns-b5494cbf4-nnmc6 are Running with ready=true and restartCount 0, so DNS pod availability is not the observed fault.

The fault is in the shipping-to-quote request path rather than in quote's application or resources: shipping's calls hang at or near connection establishment and mostly never reach the quote handler, because quote's own handler spans stay at <=10ms while ~80% of shipping's attempts fail after 5-10s and quote's receipt rate falls from ~40/min to ~9/min at a roughly constant attempt rate; the pre-handler waiting implied by the fast handler spans cannot be observed directly (there is no accept-queue or socket metric).

Packet loss/retransmission on the path from shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 (node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e) to the quote endpoints is a candidate mechanism: successful 'POST quote' calls during the incident are spread up to the 5s ceiling (17.46 of 23.28 above 1.4s) while every failure is 5-10s, a pattern consistent with TCP retransmission/backoff rather than application queueing, and both quote endpoints (same node and different node i-0f88eaa39b314c60b) are starved. This cannot be confirmed because no packet, retransmit, conntrack or node-CPU metric exists in this Prometheus.

A slow or lossy name resolution of the hostname 'quote' could produce the same symptom, because shipping dials the hostname http://quote:8080 per new connection while other hops use long-lived gRPC channels, and a resolver timeout would delay or fail exactly this hop without any quote-side span. This is unverified: no coredns_*/dns_* metric exists in this Prometheus and shipping emits no dns.lookup span (unlike payment).

quote was not failing on its own requests: no status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR series exists for service_name="quote" (only STATUS_CODE_UNSET), its POST /getquote spans are 20.9/23.3 within 2ms and 22.1/23.3 within 10ms during the incident, and its logs contain only 'Calculated quote' lines with no error text, so the failures are attributed to the hop, not to quote's handler.

Neither party of the failing hop was resource-exhausted at the measured level: quote used ~0.0009 cores of a 5m limit with a throttling ratio that fell from 0.125 to 0.024 during the incident and held 17-18MB of a 40Mi limit, shipping used ~0.001 cores of a 5m limit with 3.3-3.7MB of 15Mi, and all nodes reported Ready with no MemoryPressure, DiskPressure or PIDPressure.

The quote Deployment's cpu 5m / memory 40Mi limits (and shipping's cpu 5m / 15Mi limits) are not the cause of the 5-10s failures: quote used about 0.9 millicores of its 5-millicore quota and 17-18MB of 40Mi, its CFS throttling ratio decreased during the incident (0.125 at 17:42:24 to 0.024 at 17:53:24 for quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b), and its in-process handler spans stayed at <=2ms for 20.9 of 23.3 calls, which excludes CPU starvation of the handler.

A traffic ramp overwhelming the stack is not supported: frontend span rate was flat at 53.5-54.8 spans/s from 17:24:00 to 17:42:00 (and only fell afterwards), and shipping's quote attempt volume was ~200 per 5m before the incident versus 123-195 per 5m after, so the errors began without an increase in load on this path.

A quote rollout, scale event or pod restart at the incident is not the cause: quote has a single ReplicaSet quote-6b5877698d created 17:06:14 with 2/2 ready, both quote pods have restartCount 0, and every otel-demo pod was created 17:06:14-17:06:16, i.e. 36 minutes before the 17:42 error onset with no restart in between; no controller SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete events for quote appear in the event window.

gaps: Jaeger's newest trace is from 17:26:30, ~32 minutes before the alert, and searches inside 17:43:00-17:44:00 returned no traces (a no_data result), so the incident-period spans, their status tags and error detail text are unknown; the exact client error (deadline exceeded vs connection reset vs DNS failure) is not observable.

No container_network_* series and no node CPU, load or conntrack metrics exist in this Prometheus, so packet loss, retransmission, accept-queue depth and sender-node saturation cannot be measured or excluded.
No coredns_*/dns_* metric exists and shipping emits no dns.lookup span, so the name-resolution hypothesis cannot be tested; only pod-level CoreDNS liveness was checked.

http_server_request_duration_seconds_count has no series in the window (get_all_labels returned no data), so the HTTP status codes returned to frontend-proxy and load-generator (e.g. 500 vs 503) are unknown.
list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data, so the alert expression, threshold and evaluation window could not be verified against the reported value 1.111111.

Error-pattern searches of the shipping and checkout container logs returned no matching lines (a no_data result after reading 1069 and 573 lines respectively), which does not prove absence; the application's error text for these timeouts was not obtained.
kube_pod_container_info returned no data for the quote pods, so image digests (possible config drift between the two replicas) could not be compared.
No NetworkPolicy objects were returned for otel-demo (a no_data result), so the absence of a policy affecting shipping-to-quote traffic is not proven.

No HorizontalPodAutoscaler objects were returned for otel-demo (a no_data result), so autoscaling activity cannot be ruled in or out from that source; the 2/2 ready Deployment status is the only scaling evidence observed.
The change_history integration is not available, so no deployment or configuration change record explains the 17:42 onset.
The origin of the ~1/minute Normal 'Updated' events on both quote pods and of the ~1/minute quote requests at :21-:26 is unidentified.
Whether requests queue in the quote accept path (php-fpm/sidecar) or are dropped on the wire could not be distinguished; no accept-queue, socket or process-level metric is available.
next_steps: Capture a short packet trace and a DNS query log from shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 while the failure is active, to distinguish resolver timeout, SYN retransmission and server accept delay.
Inspect Cilium/Hubble and conntrack counters on node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e for drops, table pressure and retransmits toward 100.96.2.155:8080 and 100.96.4.53:8080 during 17:42-17:58.
Enable container_network_* and node CPU/conntrack metrics (or a scrape of the CNI) so this class of hop failure is measurable next time.
Add readiness probes to quote and shipping, and HTTP status/error metrics at the quote endpoint, so accept-path failures surface as readiness or 5xx rather than only as client timeouts.
Retain or forward Jaeger traces with a shorter ingestion delay (currently ~32 minutes behind) so incident-window spans and error details are retrievable.
Review the tight limits (quote cpu 5m/40Mi, shipping cpu 5m/15Mi) as hygiene, while noting the measured usage shows they are not the cause of this incident.

hypothesis.text: The fault is in the shipping-to-quote request path rather than in quote's application or resources: shipping's calls hang at or near connection establishment and mostly never reach the quote handler, because quote's own handler spans stay at <=10ms while ~80% of shipping's attempts fail after 5-10s and quote's receipt rate falls from ~40/min to ~9/min at a roughly constant attempt rate; the pre-handler waiting implied by the fast handler spans cannot be observed directly (there is no accept-queue or socket metric).

Packet loss/retransmission on the path from shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 (node i-0b3bc2b3bf9ce710e) to the quote endpoints is a candidate mechanism: successful 'POST quote' calls during the incident are spread up to the 5s ceiling (17.46 of 23.28 above 1.4s) while every failure is 5-10s, a pattern consistent with TCP retransmission/backoff rather than application queueing, and both quote endpoints (same node and different node i-0f88eaa39b314c60b) are starved. This cannot be confirmed because no packet, retransmit, conntrack or node-CPU metric exists in this Prometheus.

A slow or lossy name resolution of the hostname 'quote' could produce the same symptom, because shipping dials the hostname http://quote:8080 per new connection while other hops use long-lived gRPC channels, and a resolver timeout would delay or fail exactly this hop without any quote-side span. This is unverified: no coredns_*/dns_* metric exists in this Prometheus and shipping emits no dns.lookup span (unlike payment).

counter_evidence.text: quote was not failing on its own requests: no status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR series exists for service_name="quote" (only STATUS_CODE_UNSET), its POST /getquote spans are 20.9/23.3 within 2ms and 22.1/23.3 within 10ms during the incident, and its logs contain only 'Calculated quote' lines with no error text, so the failures are attributed to the hop, not to quote's handler.

Neither party of the failing hop was resource-exhausted at the measured level: quote used ~0.0009 cores of a 5m limit with a throttling ratio that fell from 0.125 to 0.024 during the incident and held 17-18MB of a 40Mi limit, shipping used ~0.001 cores of a 5m limit with 3.3-3.7MB of 15Mi, and all nodes reported Ready with no MemoryPressure, DiskPressure or PIDPressure.

rejected_hypothesis.text: The quote Deployment's cpu 5m / memory 40Mi limits (and shipping's cpu 5m / 15Mi limits) are not the cause of the 5-10s failures: quote used about 0.9 millicores of its 5-millicore quota and 17-18MB of 40Mi, its CFS throttling ratio decreased during the incident (0.125 at 17:42:24 to 0.024 at 17:53:24 for quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b), and its in-process handler spans stayed at <=2ms for 20.9 of 23.3 calls, which excludes CPU starvation of the handler.

A traffic ramp overwhelming the stack is not supported: frontend span rate was flat at 53.5-54.8 spans/s from 17:24:00 to 17:42:00 (and only fell afterwards), and shipping's quote attempt volume was ~200 per 5m before the incident versus 123-195 per 5m after, so the errors began without an increase in load on this path.

A quote rollout, scale event or pod restart at the incident is not the cause: quote has a single ReplicaSet quote-6b5877698d created 17:06:14 with 2/2 ready, both quote pods have restartCount 0, and every otel-demo pod was created 17:06:14-17:06:16, i.e. 36 minutes before the 17:42 error onset with no restart in between; no controller SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete events for quote appear in the event window.
